problem:
Consider the straight line with the parametric equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2+4t \\ y=5+5t \\ z=-1+6t\end{aligned}
$$

for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ Find the Cartesian equation of this line.
worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2+4t \\ 5+5t \\ -1+6t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ 5t \\ 6t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ 6\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $P(2,5,-1)$ and is parallel to the vector $v=⟨4,5,6⟩.$ So, its Cartesian (canonical) equation is given by

$$
\frac{x-2}{4}=\frac{y-5}{5}=\frac{z-(-1)}{6}=t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Simplifying, we reach

$$
\frac{x-2}{4}=\frac{y-5}{5}=\frac{z+1}{6}.
$$
